notes: rounds/tester.py result() does every check in one transaction (POST holds the round lock): non-Open round, superseded build, the tester's own result and a POST to a submitted result; it passes the fetched row to services.save_result, which raises ResultSubmitted for a submitted one, and result.html shows a submitted result without a form. M1's single read edit both shows and overwrites another tester's result; M4 removes the view and service checks and lets result.html show the form (status still Submitted). ResultForm.clean requires a Fail observation, backed by the CheckConstraint rounds_result_fail_has_observation, which M2 removes from the model and migration 0005_result together (otherwise the save fails with a 503); ObservationField(max_length=2000) limits it, so M5's message also says 2001. M3 leaves the tester round page's Open-only 'Record result' link in place (navigation, not a guard). M5 also widens the model field and its column in migration 0005_result to 2001, together, because the varchar(2000) column would otherwise refuse the save (a 503) and a model-only change would fail the candidate's makemigrations --check test; pytest-django builds the test database from migrations on every run (no --reuse-db), so the migration edit is seen consistently.
